FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Moderate joint effusion with mild synovial thickening. Tiny amount of fluid in the pes anserine bursa. No popliteal cyst.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
There is a peripheral vertical tear involving the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. It is located 3 mm from meniscocapsular junction.
Mild diffuse cartilage fraying with focal partial-thickness cartilage fissuring at the medial femoral articular surface without subchondral bone marrow reactive changes.
Mild thickening of the proximal medial collateral ligament injury with mild superficial edema, suggesting healing low-grade sprain.
Mild tendinosis of the semimembranosus tendon near its femoral insertion.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
No tear of the lateral meniscus.
Mild thinning of the lateral femoral condyle cartilage without full-thickness chondral loss. No subchondral bone marrow reactive changes.
Abnormal thickening of the distal conjoint ligament, suggesting a subacute low-grade injury.
There is edema of the popliteus muscle with a small intramuscular cystic change, in keeping with grade 2 strain. Its tendon remains within normal limits without tear.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
There is complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament in its midportion. The posterior cruciate ligament is normal.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Deep cartilage fissuring in the medial and lateral facets patella without subchondral bone marrow reactive changes.
Unremarkable extensor tendons and patellar retinacula.

Bones:
Bone contusions in the posterior aspect of the bilateral tibial plateau.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
As above.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:
1.Complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament.
2.Vertical peripheral tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus.
3.Low-grade subacute injury of the medial collateral ligament and distal conjoined lateral ligament.
4.Grade 2 injury of the popliteus muscle belly without tendon tear.
5.Areas of mild cartilage thinning and varying degrees of cartilage fissures as described above
6.Bone contusions in the bilateral tibial plateaux.
7.Moderate joint effusion and mild synovitis.

Fluid:

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Longitudinal horizontal tear at the junction of the body and anterior horn extending through the anterior horn and root, with loss of meniscal volume and parameniscal cyst measuring approximately up to 1 cm maximally in transverse dimension.
Mild thinning of articular cartilage. Normal lateral collateral ligament complex.

Mild mucoid degeneration of the ACL. Normal PCL.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Patella baja (Insall Salvati ratio 0.7).
Partial-thickness chondral thinning within the medial patellar facet articular cartilage (grade 2 chondrosis). Small marginal osteophytes in keeping with mild osteoarthrosis. Normal fat pads.

Bones:
Normal.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

Anterior horn/body lateral meniscal tear, with associated parameniscal cyst.

MRI LEFT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
Left knee pain and stiffness. Ultrasound shows a large complex collection at the posterior joint, MRI suggested. 

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
Ultrasound report dated [Date]

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: intact

Medial meniscus: Several tears of the medial meniscus noted. Radial tear close to the posterior root of the medial meniscus and another inferior surfacing horizontal tear is seen at the posterior horn. Radial tear with truncation also seen at the body of meniscus, which is attenuated in size. Most of the medial meniscus is extruded from the jointline, approximately 0.4cm medial to joint line. 

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: intact

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. Thickening of the superificial component of the medial collateral ligament with moderate periligamentous edema is suggestive of moderate sprain. 

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

Moderate knee effusion noted with evidence of synovitis. Thinned wall Baker's cyst with thin septations measuring 4.1cm x 3.4cm x 6.1cm (TSxAPxCC) is seen, consistent with a complex Bakers cyst. No fluid fluid level is seen..Small amount of fluid at the posterior knee is probably secondary to previous rupture.

Mild prepatellar bursitis observed. 

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: Mild oedema is seen at the anterior aspect of the medial tibial plateau. Moderate degenerative changes with osteophytosis of all three compartments noted. No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Full thickness chondral loss and fissures most observable at the patella apex and medial patella facet, associated with subchondral oedema. 

Medial compartment: Minimal chondrosis. 

Lateral compartment: Minimal chondrosis. 

Others:

Hoffas fat pad: clear

Muscles: Severe atrophy and fatty infiltration of the semimembranosus muscle. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT

1.	Multiloculated Bakers cyst with prior rupture. No evidence of haemorrhage or active inflammatory changes. 
2.	Several tears of the medial meniscus, including a radial tear of the posterior root, horizontal tear of the posterior horn and truncation of the inner free edge of the body of medial meniscus. Medial meniscal extrusion noted. 
3.	Moderate sprain of the superficial component of the medial collateral ligament. It is intact with no tear. 
4.	Severe patellofemoral chondral loss and fissures with subchondral oedema. Otherwise only minimal chondrosis at the tibiofemoral joint. Osteophytes in all three compartments.
5.	Mild prepatellar bursitis.
